definition: Wikidata is a collaboratively edited multilingual knowledge graph hosted by the Wikimedia Foundation.
details: It is a source of open data released under the Creative Commons CC0 public domain dedication. It is for the use of both Wikimedia and external projects. Wikidata is a wiki powered by the software MediaWiki, including its extension for semi-structured data, the Wikibase. As of early 2025, Wikidata had 1.65 billion item statements (semantic triples).

explainer.lead: Wikidata is a collaboratively edited multilingual knowledge graph hosted by the Wikimedia Foundation and released as open data under CC0. It matters as a shared source of structured facts for both Wikimedia and external projects.

tiers.eli5: It is a giant public database of facts that anyone can edit, and other apps can look things up in it.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers query it for structured entities and relationships, backed by MediaWiki and its Wikibase extension for semi-structured data. A pitfall is that open collaborative editing means coverage and consistency vary by topic.
tiers.paperLevel: A knowledge graph stored as semantic triples (item statements). As of early 2025 it held 1.65 billion item statements; its scope and accuracy are bounded by contributor coverage.

explainer.example: An app looks up a city's population and country by querying the corresponding Wikidata items and their statements.
